fields.explanation: The original group C2, four indices, crossed two-block partitions, constant b=1 and a=(1,1,1,g) are preserved. The source local counting passage assumes an arbitrary finite group and n>=2; its later nonabelian-simple application is not an assumption of this passage. Mathlib Multiplicative(ZMod2), Setoid.ker, lattice meet/join and quotient cardinalities implement the actual objects. The partition meet is bottom (singletons), so the source ratio hypothesis holds; the join is top with one class, giving claimed count2. Group cancellation proves there are no block-constant pairs satisfying the four product equations, and Nat.card of the complete solution subtype is zero. The refutation concerns precisely this local counting claim.
fields.flaw: Whenever the ratios $a_i b_i^{-1}$ agree on parts of $\pi\wedge\sigma$, the equations $u_i v_i=a_i b_i^{-1}$, with $u$ constant on parts of $\pi$ and $v$ constant on parts of $\sigma$, have exactly $|G|^{|\pi\vee\sigma|}$ solutions.

fields.witness: Let G=C2={1,g}, g²=1, on indices {1,2,3,4}. Take π={{1,2},{3,4}}, σ={{1,3},{2,4}}, b_i=1, and (a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4)=(1,1,1,g). Then π∧σ consists of singletons, so the ratios a_i b_i⁻¹ satisfy the hypothesis. Also π∨σ has one part, so the claimed count is 2.
